title: Callvale after: an Application Load Balancer in three zones
claim: Users reach an Application Load Balancer with a node in three zones, and it sends requests to the healthy web instances in private subnets.
alt: After: users connect over HTTPS to an Application Load Balancer in public subnets in AZ 1, AZ 2 and AZ 3. It forwards requests to one web instance in a private subnet in each zone. The instance in AZ 2 is marked unhealthy and gets no requests.

edges.label: HTTPS
edges.say: Users connect over HTTPS to the load balancer's DNS name.

edges.label: certificate
edges.say: The HTTPS listener uses an ACM certificate to terminate the front-end connection.
A node in each Availability Zone selects a healthy registered target from the target group.
Health checks find the failed instance, and the load balancer routes traffic only to the healthy targets.
The instances' security group names the load balancer's security group as the source, so they receive traffic exclusively from the load balancer.

notes: Brief 14 story pair, after; 2-deep.md#decision-record (after Decision). Title, claim, alt, steps from brief.json. Two columns (three do not fit a phone); one private subnet per zone on the right. Zones are named in labels (three zone boxes exceed the limit). No Auto Scaling group, CloudFront, Route 53 or WAF. Step facts in the Markdown per brief facts_for_steps; step 5 links elb-target-sg-reference-lb-sg. No AWS number in the drawing.
